A.title: FLY LOW
A.hint: Clear pictures. Planes Havana can shoot at.
A.aftermath: Navy reconnaissance squadrons in Florida are put on alert.

B.title: KEEP WATCHING
B.hint: Stay high. Stay quiet. Stay unsure.
B.aftermath: The analysts ask for more time. They always do.

A.title: SMALL CIRCLE
A.hint: Fewer leaks. Fewer voices in the room.
A.aftermath: A dozen men start meeting in the Cabinet Room. The press is told nothing.

B.title: WIDEN THE ROOM
B.hint: More support. More people who know.
B.aftermath: Cabinet secretaries are briefed by evening. One of them talks to his wife.

A.title: CALL IT INTOLERABLE
A.hint: A public line. Hard to step back from.
A.aftermath: The press office drafts a statement. It cannot be unsaid.

B.title: SAY NOTHING YET
B.hint: Room to move. Time to lose.
B.aftermath: The schedule stays normal. Tomorrow the President campaigns in Connecticut.

A.title: READY THE STRIKE
A.hint: Fastest to use. Hardest to take back.
A.aftermath: Tactical Air Command starts moving aircraft to bases in Florida.

B.title: READY A BLOCKADE
B.hint: Ships instead of bombs. Slower. Louder.
B.aftermath: Navy staff start writing the rules for stopping a Soviet ship.

A.title: TALK TO HAVANA
A.hint: A quiet channel. Castro may not want it.
A.aftermath: A message is drafted for the Brazilian ambassador in Havana.

B.title: MOSCOW'S PROBLEM
B.hint: One adversary. One address.
B.aftermath: Cuba drops off the agenda. In Havana, someone notices.

A.title: SHARE THE EVIDENCE
A.hint: Allies on board. Secrets in more hands.
A.aftermath: Dean Acheson is told to pack a folder of photographs for Paris.

B.title: KEEP IT SECRET
B.hint: Full control. Allies left guessing.
B.aftermath: The allies will hear it on the radio, like everyone else.

A.title: STRIKE BEFORE THEY'RE READY
A.hint: Act now, while the sites are unfinished.
A.aftermath: The Joint Chiefs are told to plan for the earliest possible date.

B.title: GIVE THEM AN EXIT
B.hint: Pressure first. Force held in reserve.
B.aftermath: In the drafts, the word 'blockade' starts turning into 'quarantine'.

A.title: MISSILES ONLY
A.hint: Smaller strike. Their defenses stay up.
A.aftermath: The target list is cut to the launch sites. The Air Force says it will do its best.

B.title: THE WHOLE PACKAGE
B.hint: Airfields, SAMs, then an invasion force.
B.aftermath: Troops start moving toward Florida. The Chiefs finally look satisfied.

A.title: QUARANTINE TO TALK
A.hint: Buy time. Leave Khrushchev a door.
A.aftermath: Stevenson is told to prepare the case for the United Nations.

B.title: QUARANTINE AND ULTIMATUM
B.hint: Set a clock. Say it out loud.
B.aftermath: A deadline is written into the draft. Someone underlines it twice.

A.title: WEAPONS ONLY
A.hint: Narrow. Defensible. Leaves them room.
A.aftermath: The proclamation lists missiles, bombers and warheads. Nothing else.

B.title: EVERYTHING, FUEL INCLUDED
B.hint: Squeezes Cuba. Looks like an act of war.
B.aftermath: Tankers bound for Havana are added to the list. Moscow notices first.

A.title: PULL IT IN
A.hint: More time for Moscow. Less margin for us.
A.aftermath: The Navy redraws the line. Admiral Anderson is not pleased.

B.title: KEEP IT FAR
B.hint: Safer for our ships. Faster to collide.
B.aftermath: The destroyers take their positions. The clock starts sooner.

A.title: DEMAND WITHDRAWAL
A.hint: Clear. Popular. Hard to walk back.
A.aftermath: At seven, the country hears the word 'withdrawal'. So does Moscow.

B.title: DEMAND A FREEZE
B.hint: Room to bargain. Looks softer on TV.
B.aftermath: At seven, the country hears the word 'halt'. Some commentators call it weak.

A.title: OPEN A BACK CHANNEL
A.hint: Say privately what you can't say publicly.
A.aftermath: Robert Kennedy calls the Soviet embassy and asks for a quiet meeting.

B.title: OFFICIAL CHANNELS ONLY
B.hint: Nothing said that can't be printed.
B.aftermath: Everything goes through State. Every word is on the record.

A.title: AUTOMATIC RETALIATION
A.hint: Fast response. Nobody asks you first.
A.aftermath: The rule goes down the chain of command. It will not come back up.

B.title: NOTHING WITHOUT MY ORDER
B.hint: Slower. Every shot goes through you.
B.aftermath: The rule goes down the chain: no retaliation without the President.

A.title: GO TO DEFCON 2
A.hint: Maximum readiness. Minimum margin.
A.aftermath: General Power announces the alert in the clear. Moscow hears every word.

B.title: HOLD AT DEFCON 3
B.hint: Serious, not maximal. Room to step back.
B.aftermath: The alert stays where it is. Some generals call that hesitation.

A.title: CALL IT OFF
A.hint: Recall every squadron. If they can hear you.
A.aftermath: The recall reaches every squadron. The runways go quiet.
A.aftermath_if_failed: The recall reaches most squadrons. Not all of them.

B.title: LET THEM GO
B.hint: The strike proceeds as ordered.
B.aftermath: Engines start across Florida. There is no second button.

A.title: STOP AND BOARD
A.hint: Enforce the line. Risk the submarine.
A.aftermath: Rusk, quietly: 'We're eyeball to eyeball.' Nobody knows yet who will blink.

B.title: LET HER PASS, FOLLOW
B.hint: Avoid contact. Look like you blinked.
B.aftermath: The freighter crosses the line. In Congress, someone asks what the line is for.

A.title: PROMISE NOT TO INVADE
A.hint: Give him the way out he asked for.
A.aftermath: A reply is drafted. It says 'no invasion' in plain words.

B.title: NO GUARANTEES
B.hint: Withdrawal first. Promises never.
B.aftermath: The reply says nothing about Cuba's future. Moscow waits for a second answer.

A.title: ACCEPT IN PUBLIC
A.hint: End it now. Pay with the alliance.
A.aftermath: In Ankara, the government asks why it heard it on the radio.

B.title: REJECT IN PUBLIC
B.hint: No trades under pressure.
B.aftermath: The rejection is broadcast. The deadline is not.

A.title: HOLD AND VERIFY
A.hint: Find out who fired, and why.
A.aftermath: The strike is held. The pilot was Major Rudolf Anderson.
A.aftermath_if_failed: The hold order arrives late. The first aircraft have already fired.

B.title: EXECUTE RETALIATION
B.hint: Hit the site. Answer fire with fire.
B.aftermath: Four aircraft cross into Cuban airspace. In Moscow, it is already night.

A.title: ACCEPT THE PAUSE
A.hint: Both sides freeze. For now.
A.aftermath: Forces hold on both sides. Nobody calls it a ceasefire.
A.locked_text: No channel can carry it in time.

B.title: CALL IT A TRICK
B.hint: Keep the pressure. Assume the worst.
B.aftermath: The pause is refused. On both sides, the clocks start again.

A.title: MAKE THE PROMISE
A.hint: Secret concession. Deniable. Binding.
A.aftermath: Robert Kennedy leaves for the Justice Department. Nothing is written down.

B.title: KEEP TURKEY OUT
B.hint: No link. No leak. No deal.
B.aftermath: The meeting covers Cuba only. Dobrynin asks twice about Turkey.

A.title: RECOGNIZE AND NEGOTIATE
A.hint: Talk to Havana as Havana.
A.aftermath: A cable goes to Rio. Nobody in Moscow is copied.

B.title: KEEP HIM ISOLATED
B.hint: No deals with Castro. Ever.
B.aftermath: Havana gets no answer. Castro gives a speech instead.

A.title: INSPECT AND WATCH
A.hint: Accept what can be verified.
A.aftermath: The first photographs show crates on the docks.
A.aftermath_if_failed: Moscow stalls on the details. The crates don't move.

B.title: FULL ACCESS NOW
B.hint: Everything, immediately, or nothing.
B.aftermath: Moscow accepts, grudgingly. The crates start moving.
B.aftermath_if_failed: Moscow calls the demand humiliating. The announcement is 'under review'.

A.title: STAND DOWN
A.hint: Signal it's over. Trust the deal.
A.aftermath: The bombers come home. General LeMay calls it a defeat.

B.title: STAY READY
B.hint: Keep the pressure until it's done.
B.aftermath: The alert stays up. So does the tension, for weeks.

A.title: GRANT ACCESS
A.hint: For the peace, apparently.
A.aftermath: A desk is cleared in the West Wing. The Secret Service asks for it in writing.

B.title: HANG UP
B.hint: Some doors stay closed.
B.aftermath: The line goes dead. The operator writes it down anyway.

A.title: SIGN IT
A.hint: Peace, at a very strange price.
A.aftermath: The ink dries. Somewhere, a portrait is quietly replaced.

B.title: DISSOLVE IT
B.hint: The Constitution is not negotiable.
B.aftermath: The coalition dissolves. Nobody admits having joined it.
